numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For a single-point grid (points=([0],[0]), values=np.array([[0]])) with method='linear', calling rgi([[0,0]]) returns array([nan]) for float64 values; the float32 variant returns array([0.]) correctly. The NaN came from an unnecessary branch in the linear 2D Cython evaluator (scipy/interpolate/_rgi_cython.pyx) that set out[point] = NAN.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: rgi([[0,0]]) should return array([0.]) for the float64 single-point 2D grid, matching the float32 result and the value at the grid point.
trigger_conditions: 2D grid with a single point (each axis of length 1)

numerical_characteristics.dtype: float64 and float32 (single-point 2D grid bug observed in float64; reproducer uses float32 values)
category_specific_evidence: Commit message: test_length_one_axes[linear-2-float64] fails as of commit 4c1a4da81 while all other parametrizations pass, per the commit text.
PR body: for a 2D, float64 grid with a single point, a NaN is returned by linear interpolation; the fix explicitly handles the single grid point on both axes.
Issue #23171 reproducer: RegularGridInterpolator(points=([0],[0]), values=np.array([[0]], dtype=np.float32), method='linear') called at [[0,0]] returns array([0.]) as expected.
Cython diff: the single-point-on-both-axes branch sets out[point] = values[0, 0]; the NAN branches were removed because out-of-bounds/NaN points are handled by the caller.

Test parametrization covers dtype float32/float64, ndim 1/2/3, and methods linear/nearest, with expected values like 1/7 (val) and fill value 1/42 in a later test version; the discussion notes the expected single-point behaviour is that the result equals the grid value.
Discussion of test_length_one_axes shows values constructed as np.full of shape (1,)*ndim filled with 1/7 in dtype.
reproduction_risks: The original failing case is 2D float64 with linear method; the float32 reproducer in the issue may not trigger the NaN, so both dtypes and ndim=2 should be tested.
Test names differ between passages (test_length_one_axes vs test_length_one_axis_all), so the reproduction should not rely on a specific name.
Points passed as nested lists versus arrays may matter (the reproducer uses [[0,0]] as the query).
